answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly and reputation earned. Imagine agents registered at a small grove of trusted issuers, each staking real value, with peer reviewers scattered like a cedar stand on a knoll: every new agent must be countersigned by established members before it earns rewards. Because each endorsement is scarce and slashable, flooding the network with fake agents becomes more expensive than the mining income those fakes could capture.
